title: Operational theory for photonic circuits: generalizing linear optics beyond quantum theory
authors: Ismaël Septembre, Matthias Kleinmann, Martin Plávala
abstract: We use the analogy between the quadrature operators in quantum optics and the phase-space coordinates in a mechanical harmonic oscillator to generalise the theory of linear optics beyond quantum theory. For this, we introduce a framework for analysing photonic circuits within generalised probabilistic theories based on quadrature operators. Using this framework, we ask whether phenomena like the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometry are specific to quantum theory or also occur across a broader class of theories. We find the latter: the vanishing photon coincidences at the output of a beam splitter also occur for classical light and for a modified version of quantised light. Similarly, for Mach-Zehnder interferometry we find that there is no qualitative difference between quantum theory and these alternative theories. Our framework can serve as a foundation to study generalised theories of complex photonic set-ups and photonic quantum computers.
summary: This paper generalizes linear optics theory by mapping quantum quadrature operators onto classical phase-space coordinates. It investigates fundamental quantum phenomena like the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect and MZI using this generalized framework. The key finding is that these interference effects persist across classical and alternative theories, suggesting a broader physical principle governs them.
main_problem: To generalize the theory of linear optics beyond quantum mechanics by developing a framework based on quadrature operators and analyzing interference phenomena.
main_result: The vanishing of photon coincidences at a beam splitter and the behavior of Mach-Zehnder interferometry are found to occur in both classical and modified quantized theories, suggesting these effects are general features of the generalized framework.
method: The authors use an analogy between quantum quadrature operators and phase-space coordinates, developing a generalized probabilistic theory framework using pseudo-probability distributions on phase space.
model_or_system: The study focuses on photonic circuits involving linear optical elements like beam splitters and phase shifters, modeled using two coupled harmonic oscillators in phase space.
key_observables: Coincidence probability ($P_{co}$), visibility ($V$), and the joint numerical range of coincidence vs. Hadamard coincidence measurements.
important_parameters: Relative phase ($	heta_{rel}$), energy threshold ($E_{th}$), and the comparison between classical, quantum, and sawtooth theory limits.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the generalized framework using quadrature operators, applying it to fundamental linear optical setups (HOM, MZI), and culminating in a comparison of predictions across classical, quantum, and alternative theories, including contextuality tests.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the foundations of quantum optics by testing the necessity of quantum mechanics for observed photonic phenomena, which is highly relevant for understanding photonic quantum computing architectures.
